speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your sudden lower back pain and leg radiation in detail, including when it started, what makes it better or worse, and if you have any numbness or weakness. To begin our assessment, please tell me your age and if you have any history of back problems, trauma, or recent heavy lifting.

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you. Based on your age and the sudden onset of sharp pain radiating down your leg to the foot after exercise, I suspect a disc herniation. Can you tell me if you have any numbness, tingling, or weakness in that leg, and specifically which toe or part of the foot is affected? Also, does coughing or sneezing make the pain worse?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lumbar Disc Herniation (L5 or S1 radiculopathy).

The clinical picture of acute onset back pain radiating to the foot during exercise, coupled with worsening pain on movement, is highly suggestive of a herniated disc compressing a nerve root. Given the absence of reported numbness, weakness, or exacerbation by Valsalva maneuvers (coughing/sneezing) in your latest update, I am confident in this conclusion without further testing.
